extracted_by: claude-opus-5-5 SV-G2 blind second extraction S1
article_notes: 40 dogs with PCR-confirmed B. canis canis (Zagreb faculty clinic) plus 30 healthy controls. Samples taken on the day of admission; the article does not state whether before or after the imidocarb dose (presumably before). Severity groups: uncomplicated (29), one complication (6), MODS (5) by Table 1 criteria; 4 MODS dogs died. Group comparisons are pairwise Mann-Whitney; significance between groups is shown by table superscript letters (Tables 3-5), checked against the Results text. Table 2 (control vs babesiosis) skipped as infected vs healthy. Table 6 correlations of oxidative markers with routine analytes (urea, bilirubin, CPK, etc.) are marker-marker correlations and were not extracted, except HCT (degree of anaemia, extracted under S7). Table 5 superscripts also compare mild and moderate anaemia with non-anaemic dogs; only the moderate vs mild contrast named in the text was extracted. Severely anaemic group (n=1) not analysed by the authors.

not_extracted.what: Descriptive statistics of routine biochemistry and haematology parameters (Additional file 1)
not_extracted.note: Unclear whether the supplement splits these by severity group.

severity_definitions.label: MODS vs uncomplicated babesiosis
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs with dysfunction of 2 or more organs (MODS) vs dogs with none of the Table 1 complications (renal creatinine >180 umol/L, respiratory, hepatic, muscular CPK >600 U/L, CNS modified Glasgow coma scale <9).
severity_definitions.quote: On the basis of clinical manifestations and laboratory data the affected dogs were divided into two groups: uncomplicated and complicated babesiosis, whereas the complicated group was further subdivided into those with one complication and the MODS group, due to the criteria listed in Table 1.
severity_definitions.definition_source: author-defined (Table 1 criteria; Welzl et al. Glasgow coma scale)

severity_definitions.label: MODS vs one complication
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs with MODS vs dogs with a single organ dysfunction (Table 1 criteria).
severity_definitions.quote: On the basis of clinical manifestations and laboratory data the affected dogs were divided into two groups: uncomplicated and complicated babesiosis, whereas the complicated group was further subdivided into those with one complication and the MODS group, due to the criteria listed in Table 1.

severity_definitions.label: one complication vs uncomplicated
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs with a single organ dysfunction vs uncomplicated dogs (Table 1 criteria; muscular involvement = rhabdomyolysis component).
severity_definitions.quote: On the basis of clinical manifestations and laboratory data the affected dogs were divided into two groups: uncomplicated and complicated babesiosis, whereas the complicated group was further subdivided into those with one complication and the MODS group, due to the criteria listed in Table 1.

severity_definitions.label: lethal outcome
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs that died despite treatment (all had MODS) vs survivors; correlation of markers with lethal outcome by Kendall Tau-b. Euthanasia not mentioned.
severity_definitions.quote: Treatment was successful in all dogs without development of any complications as well as in 7 cases of complicated babesiosis, while 4 dogs with MODS died despite treatment (mortality rate 10%).

severity_definitions.label: anaemic vs non-anaemic
severity_definitions.definition: Anaemic (HCT <=37%) vs non-anaemic (HCT >37%) dogs with babesiosis.
severity_definitions.quote: Additionally, the babesiosis group was divided according to the degree of anaemia (on the basis of haematocrit - HCT percentage) into non-anaemic: HCT >37%, mildly anaemic: 30–37%, moderately anaemic: 18–29% and severely anaemic: <18% dogs.

severity_definitions.label: moderately vs mildly anaemic
severity_definitions.definition: Moderately anaemic (HCT 18-29%) vs mildly anaemic (HCT 30-37%) dogs; the one severely anaemic dog was not analysed.
severity_definitions.quote: Additionally, the babesiosis group was divided according to the degree of anaemia (on the basis of haematocrit - HCT percentage) into non-anaemic: HCT >37%, mildly anaemic: 30–37%, moderately anaemic: 18–29% and severely anaemic: <18% dogs.

severity_definitions.label: HCT (continuous degree of anaemia)
severity_definitions.definition: Haematocrit as a continuous measure of anaemia severity; Spearman correlation with each oxidative marker in the 40 dogs with babesiosis.
severity_definitions.quote: Also, there was a significant positive correlation of HCT with GPx and SOD, whereas significant negative correlation of HCT with MDA (Table 6).
